clue.text: Glutton has store holding a lot of drink

parts.note: a glutton is a hog, one who eats greedily

indicators.note: the store word holds the little word a inside it

parts.note: a shed is a place to store things

explanation.surface: A greedy eater keeps a large stock of booze in his storeroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' puts A inside SHED to make SHEAD; 'has' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A hogshead is a large cask, and so a big measured quantity of wine or beer.

clue.text: Following method, had got up — here?

definitions.text: Following method, had got up — here?

parts.note: how something is done is its method

indicators.note: in a down clue, getting up means the word had is read from bottom to top

explanation.surface: Someone climbs up onto a seat in the approved way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'got up' signals reading upwards in a down clue. The whole clue doubles as the definition: you must climb up to sit in an elephant's seat.
explanation.definitionFit: A howdah is the canopied seat on an elephant's back that riders climb up into.

clue.text: Responsible word from foreman

definitions.meaning: the jury foreman announces the verdict, often this one word

explanation.definitionFit: Being to blame for an offence is being culpable, and a jury's foreman delivers that verdict.

clue.text: Curve finally altered: that's not to be taken literally

definitions.text: that's not to be taken literally

indicators.note: the last letter of the curve word is changed for another

parts.note: a hyperbola is a curve in geometry

explanation.surface: A remark about a bend being changed at the end, said not to be meant literally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally altered' swaps the closing A of the geometric curve for E.
explanation.definitionFit: Exaggeration used for effect is meant figuratively, never as a literal statement.

clue.text: Aussies bring remarkably hard-hearted approach to the land

indicators.note: something done remarkably is out of the ordinary, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Australians introduce an unsentimental way of farming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'remarkably' rearranges the twelve letters of AUSSIES BRING.
explanation.definitionFit: Large-scale commercial farming treats the land as a business, without sentiment.

clue.text: Hood Nazis put on, forbidding looks

indicators.note: the hood is put on, wrapped inside the letters for the Nazis

parts.note: the SS was the Nazi paramilitary force
a cowl is a monk's hood

explanation.surface: Nazi troops pull on their hoods, looking menacing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put on' places COWL between the S and S.
explanation.definitionFit: Frowns of displeasure are angry, forbidding expressions on the face.

clue.text: Delightful feature of tea on motorway

indicators.note: in a down clue the tea word sits on top of the motorway letter

parts.note: char is British slang for tea
M is the abbreviation for motorway, as in M1

explanation.surface: A pleasant aspect of a cup of tea taken at a motorway service station.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' in a down clue puts CHAR above M.
explanation.definitionFit: Charm is an attractive, appealing quality, a feature that delights.

clue.text: Troy's greatness collapsed before the end

indicators.note: something that has collapsed has fallen apart, so the letters are rearranged
only the part of the fodder word before its final letter is used

explanation.surface: The glory of ancient Troy crumbled before its final fall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'before the end' drops the final S of GREATNESS; 'collapsed' rearranges GREATNES. The surface wants Homer's Troy; it is Sergeant Troy.
explanation.definitionFit: Sergeant Troy is the dashing soldier in Hardy's Far from the Madding Crowd, so the rank is Troy's title.

clue.text: Secret messages misconstrued by Chinese?

parts.note: refers to the party game Chinese ----, where a quietly passed message gets garbled along a line

explanation.definitionFit: Quiet confidential utterances are passed along the line in the party game, emerging distorted at the end.

clue.text: Maiden's emotion, laying heavenly baby here?

parts.note: M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over
anger is a strong emotion

explanation.surface: The Virgin's feelings as she lays her holy child down.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's maiden is Mary, but here it is cricket's M; the definition alludes to the infant Jesus laid in a feeding trough.
explanation.definitionFit: In the nativity story the baby Jesus was laid in a feeding trough in the stable.

clue.text: Injure Scot, admitting favouring American author

parts.note: to mar is to damage or injure

indicators.note: the Celt word lets in the following pieces

parts.note: a Scot is a Celt
pro means in favour of

explanation.surface: Hurting a Scotsman who favours the US writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'admitting' signals a container; the American in the surface is only US, and the author is French.
explanation.definitionFit: The French novelist wrote In Search of Lost Time; the clue's American is only a piece of wordplay.

clue.text: This morning sickness

parts.note: put this word ... 'morning' and the phrase means the hangover suffered the day ... drinking

explanation.definitionFit: The morning-after feeling is the queasy aftermath of a night's drinking, a kind of morning sickness.

clue.text: Smile on the lower classes? About acceptable, for them

definitions.text: Smile on the lower classes? About acceptable, for them

indicators.note: the smile word goes about the letter for acceptable

parts.note: to beam is to smile broadly
U means upper-class and so socially acceptable
D and E are the lowest social grades in British market research

explanation.surface: Would high society approve of smiling kindly on the working classes?
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' puts U inside BEAM; D and E are the bottom grades of the British social classification.
explanation.definitionFit: The fashionable elite of society is the world of the upper classes.

clue.text: Animated cartoons nice for church establishment

indicators.note: animated means lively and moving, so these letters are stirred into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Lively cartoons are thought suitable for setting up a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Animated' rearranges CARTOONS NICE; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A church is formally established when a bishop dedicates it to sacred use.

clue.text: Cold — wearing extra habit

indicators.note: the extra word wears, that is surrounds, the cold letter

parts.note: an addition is something extra
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A chill felt despite an extra monk's robe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wearing' puts C inside ADDITION. 'habit' looks like a monk's garment but is a compulsion.
explanation.definitionFit: A dependency one cannot shake off is a habit, as in a drug habit.

clue.text: Careless with punctuation?

definitions.meaning: read as slap a dash, putting in a punctuation mark

explanation.definitionFit: Work done in a hurried, sloppy way is careless; split up, it suggests slapping in a dash.

clue.text: Unworthy of father, to break into a taunt

indicators.note: the father letters break into the phrase that follows

parts.note: into gives IN, a gives A, and a taunt is a dig
FR is the abbreviation for Father, a priest's title

explanation.surface: A father would find it beneath him to start mocking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to break' puts FR into IN A DIG; 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for Latin infra dignitatem, it means beneath one's dignity, unbecoming.

clue.text: In track, bird lost footing, needing visual aid

indicators.note: the bird and the slip go in the track word

parts.note: a lane is a narrow track
a tern is a seabird
slid means lost one's footing

explanation.surface: A bird slips on a path and needs help to see.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' is the container signal, placed at the front; 'needing' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A glass slide projected by a magic lantern was an early visual aid for lectures.

clue.text: Sign, say, to pull up skirt

indicators.note: in a down clue pulling up reads the word from the bottom

parts.note: eg, for example, is what say means here
a mini is a short skirt

explanation.surface: A gesture, perhaps, to hitch up one's skirt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to pull up' turns EG into GE, followed by MINI.
explanation.definitionFit: The Twins is one of the twelve signs of the zodiac.

clue.text: Convict retains power to deceive Pom, for one

indicators.note: the convict word keeps the following pieces inside it

parts.note: a lag is a convict, as in old lag
to do someone is slang for cheating them

explanation.surface: A prisoner's power to cheat an Englishman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retains' signals a container. 'Pom' looks like Australian slang for a Briton; it is short for Pomeranian, a small dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A Pomeranian is a small pet dog of the sort kept on a lap.

clue.text: Ship's officer stores tea he's bought

indicators.note: the officer word stores the tea word inside it

parts.note: the purser keeps a ship's accounts
cha is a slang word for tea

explanation.surface: A ship's officer keeps the tea he bought on board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stores' signals a container; the definition 'he's bought' is read as 'one who has bought'.
explanation.definitionFit: A buyer is a person who has bought something, so the definition reads as a description of one.

clue.text: Stuck in such a noisy city

indicators.note: the city is stuck inside the next words, running across them

explanation.surface: Trapped in such a loud place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stuck in' signals a run of letters across 'such a noisy'.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the capital city of Vietnam.

clue.text: Secret police inspector speaking

indicators.note: spoken, the inspector word gives the letters of the answer

parts.note: a checker is one who inspects

explanation.surface: A policeman talks about undercover work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'speaking' signals a homophone of CHECKER, as said with a non-rhotic accent.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cheka was the early Soviet secret police force founded in 1917.

clue.text: Cannot be keeping daughter very interested

indicators.note: the first word keeps the daughter letter inside

parts.note: aren't, are not, says something cannot be so

explanation.surface: Someone cannot keep their daughter keen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeping' puts D inside AREN'T.
explanation.definitionFit: Being passionate and eager is being keenly interested.

clue.text: Failed in Christian obedience?

parts.note: alludes to Fletcher Christian leading the crew of HMS Bounty against Captain Bligh

explanation.definitionFit: Fletcher Christian's sailors rose against their captain, the opposite of obedience.

clue.text: Good soldier has taken out boil-in-bag meal

indicators.note: the word has takes the good soldier out with it, wrapped around him

parts.note: GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A fine soldier has eaten out on a packaged meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken out' signals a container, as one takes a date out. The dish is Scottish: offal boiled in a sheep's stomach.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scottish dish is minced offal cooked inside a sheep's stomach, a bag boiled whole.

clue.text: Having pain, full of fluid, obnoxious

indicators.note: the pain word is filled with the fluid word

parts.note: a sting is a sharp pain
ink is a writing fluid

explanation.surface: Suffering, swollen with liquid and generally unpleasant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'full of' signals a container; 'Having' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Stinking is slang for thoroughly unpleasant or offensive.
